newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss watch exports decline in January-February.
newsitem.headline: Swiss watch exports decline in January-February.

text.p: Swiss exports of watches continued to decline in 1997, falling by one percent in the first two months of the year to 1.12 billion Swiss francs, the Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry said on Monday.

Against a backdrop of a weak Swiss franc, the federation said the outlook was relatively optimistic for the rest of 1997 and that the decline appeared to have stabilised, Swiss news agency ATS reported.
Exports of Swiss watches and watch components fell 1.5 percent in 1996 to 7.55 billion Swiss francs, an improvement over a slump of 3.6 percent in 1995.
Finished watches accounted for more than 90 percent of the exports in the first two months of 1997 and were worth nearly one billion Swiss francs, ATS said, quoting federation data.
Foreign sales of all types of watches suffered nominal falls in the first two months of 1997, ATS quoted Pierre-Alain Berret, head of the industry federation's economic office, as saying.
The biggest fall in the number of units exported was in finished watches which slumped by 20 percent to five million pieces.
In a sign of consumer interest in cheaper products, exports of steel, aluminium and base metal watches rose slightly in value, the federation said, but it gave no breakdowns for sales or details.

Asia, led by Hong Kong, remained the biggest market for Swiss watches and watch components with a regional share of 41.3 percent of all foreign sales in value, followed by Europe with 35.5 percent and the United States with around 14 percent.
ATS quoted Berret as saying that prospects for global sales were favourable in 1997, notably in Asia, but that the market in Europe remained depressed.
The industry body gave no year-ago comparisons for regional sales or breakdowns for countries. Its officials were not available for comment on Monday, a public holiday.
